title: Optional IBKR data provider — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #190 (backend-ibkr-data-provider), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: app.api.dependencies.get_ibkr_provider() constructs a brand-new IBKRProvider (closed at the end of every request) on every dependency resolution, so IBKRProvider's in-memory scanner-params TTL cache and 1-req/sec run_scanner throttle never persist across requests. This is currently dormant (no route consumes get_ibkr_provider yet) but whoever builds the first consuming endpoint needs to choose a longer-lived instance (e.g. a module-level singleton, or move the cache/throttle state to a shared store) rather than assume the per-request FastAPI dependency already provides IBKR-rate-limit protection.

docs/architecture/Backend.md §3's 'Key Dependencies' table still lists `httpx` with the purpose 'via FastAPI TestClient | API integration tests' only -- it wasn't updated to also reflect that `httpx` is now a main/production runtime dependency (app/data/ibkr_provider.py's `IBKRProvider` performs real HTTP calls with it, not just tests). Update the §3 table row to mention IBKRProvider's production use alongside the existing TestClient-testing purpose.

app.api.dependencies.get_ibkr_provider()'s lazy singleton init (`if _ibkr_provider_singleton is None: _ibkr_provider_singleton = IBKRProvider(...)`) is a check-then-set on a plain module-level global with no lock, and FastAPI runs sync dependency generators in a worker thread pool -- two concurrent first-requests can both observe None and each construct their own IBKRProvider (each with independent scanner-params cache / run_scanner throttle state and its own un-closed httpx.Client), silently defeating exactly the cross-request rate-limit protection this singleton was introduced for. Consider a thread-safe lazy-init instead of hand-rolled double-checked locking -- e.g. an `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)`-wrapped factory, matching `get_settings()`'s own already-thread-safe pattern (backend/app/config.py) rather than reinventing it. Currently dormant (no route consumes get_ibkr_provider yet), found during PR #190's re-review (pr-reviewer, code-review skill sub-agent).

The module-global `_ibkr_provider_singleton` has no autouse test fixture resetting it between tests -- only the two tests that directly exercise get_ibkr_provider() remember to `monkeypatch.setattr(..., None)` first. A future test that reaches this dependency indirectly (e.g. hitting a real route through FastAPI's TestClient once one is added, rather than calling get_ibkr_provider() directly) would mutate the plain module attribute via application code's own `global` assignment -- monkeypatch's teardown only reverts changes made through monkeypatch itself, not a later in-process `global` mutation, so such a test could leak a stale IBKRProvider (bound to a previous test's base_url/mock client) into later tests in the same pytest session, non-deterministically depending on execution order. Consider an autouse fixture in tests/unit/api/test_dependencies.py (or conftest.py) that resets the singleton to None on teardown. Found during PR #190's re-review.

decisions.decision: Both non-blocking checklist items were fixed directly on PR #190's branch (task/backend-ibkr-data-provider) while addressing that PR's needs_work blocking findings, rather than through a separate branch/PR of this task's own. state is deliberately left as 'planned' rather than flipped to 'done' here.
decisions.rationale: pr-reviewer's original review comment explicitly invited fixing these 'if convenient since you're already in this area' as part of resolving the two blocking findings on the same branch -- doing so avoids a near-duplicate PR re-touching the same two files (app/api/dependencies.py, docs/architecture/Backend.md) moments later. state is left as 'planned' (not flipped to 'done') because moving a task to done -- including the git mv into docs/tasks/done/ -- is documented as pr-reviewer's/pr-merger's call once a PR is actually reviewed and merged, not task-worker's to make unilaterally; pr-reviewer re-reviewing PR #190 will see both checklist items already checked and the actual diff (get_ibkr_provider now a process-wide singleton; Backend.md §3's httpx row updated) and can move this task to done in that same pass once PR #190 merges.

decisions.decision: Replaced app.api.dependencies's plain-module-global `_ibkr_provider_singleton` + hand-rolled `if ... is None:` check-then-set with a new private `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)`-wrapped factory function `_get_ibkr_provider_singleton()` that `get_ibkr_provider()` now calls instead of touching a global directly. Updated tests/unit/api/test_dependencies.py's two tests that previously did `monkeypatch.setattr("app.api.dependencies._ibkr_provider_singleton", None)` to no longer need that (the module global no longer exists), and added a new `_reset_ibkr_provider_singleton` autouse pytest fixture in that same file that calls `_get_ibkr_provider_singleton.cache_clear()` before and after every test in the module.
decisions.rationale: This is exactly the fix the checklist item itself suggested (an lru_cache-wrapped factory matching get_settings()'s already-thread-safe pattern in app/config.py), so no alternative was seriously considered -- a hand-rolled threading.Lock double-checked-locking implementation was rejected as reinventing what functools.lru_cache already provides for a zero-argument factory. The autouse fixture placement (test_dependencies.py itself, not a shared conftest.py) mirrors this module's existing pattern of ad hoc get_settings().cache_clear() calls scattered through its own tests rather than centralizing them, since no other test module in the suite currently touches get_ibkr_provider/the IBKR singleton -- if a future test elsewhere in the suite needs the same reset (e.g. an integration test hitting a route that consumes get_ibkr_provider), it should move to a shared conftest.py fixture at that point rather than pre-emptively generalizing here for a need that doesn't exist yet. Verified: full backend test suite (890 tests), ruff, and mypy all pass on the changed files; the pre-existing ruff/mypy findings elsewhere in the backend tree (tests/unit/indicators/test_stochastic.py, tests/unit/signals/test_triple_screen.py, several tests/integration/*.py untyped-def/arg-type findings) were confirmed present on main before this change and are unrelated to this task's scope.
